synopsis: The corpus presents EUROCAE, alongside RTCA and aviation authorities, as part of the standards-based acceptance pathway for ACAS X collision-avoidance validation [f1434, f1912, f15753]. RTCA and EUROCAE published the ACAS X minimum operational performance standards DO-385 and ED-256 in October 2018 [f15747, f15371]. Chapter 2 and the glossary consistently describe this aviation precedent, but the supplied facts do not specify how its acceptance process would transfer to heavy off-road automatic braking [f1434, f1912, f15753].

relations.note: Both describe acceptance through RTCA/EUROCAE standards and aviation authorities.
Both identify RTCA, EUROCAE, and aviation authorities in ACAS X acceptance.
Both describe acceptance of collision-avoidance validation evidence through the aviation standards ecosystem.
Both report DO-385 and ED-256 publication by RTCA and EUROCAE in October 2018.
Names and dates the ACAS X standards underlying the stated acceptance pathway.
